previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis s/p gastric pacer presented with recurrent nausea and vomiting, just days after a prior discharge for similar symptoms. She had been tolerating oral intake until the morning of admission when she developed bilious, nonbloody vomiting. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and IV antiemetics including ondansetron, prochlorperazine, and ativan. Her blood pressure, elevated on presentation, was controlled with IV metoprolol and transitioned back to oral lisinopril. Laboratory evaluation showed transient leukocytosis that resolved, mild hyponatremia (Na 130-132) likely due to vomiting and inappropriate ADH, and stable renal function. Blood and urine cultures showed no true infection. She gradually improved over 36 hours, advancing to a BRAT diet and oral medications. By discharge, she was tolerating oral intake, ambulating independently, and had stable vital signs. She was discharged home with continued antiemetics, insulin management guidance, and follow-up appointments with gastroenterology for pacer evaluation and her PCP for hypertension, hyponatremia, and cardiology referral.

Brief Hospital Course:
# Nausea and vomiting - the patient presented 3 days following 
discharge from most recent admission for nausea and vomiting.  
The patient has endorsed inducing vomiting by eating/drinking 
rapidly since her last discharge to relieve her intractble 
nausea.  She was treated with NPO initially, standing PPI, 
reglan + prn compazine, zofran and ativan.  GI was consulted.  
She underwent a gastric emptying study revealing no 
gastroparesis and UGI/SBFT demonstrating normal upper GI and 
small bowel follow through without evidence for small bowel 
pathology.  As her persistent nausea was thought to be not 
completely secondary to any motility issues, we recommended head 
MRI as an outpatient to rule out central cause (e.g. 
chemoreceptor trigger zone/idiopathic intracranial hypertension 
though she has no headache or localizing neuro deficit), which 
will be set up by her PCP ___ her request.  She has 
also agreed to be seen by a psychiatrist for evaluation.  Her 
diet was advanced as tolerated to full and she was without 
vomiting for two days prior to discharge.  We added ativan 0.5 
mg po qhs as this has been helping her nausea.
.  
# DM1 / hyperglyemia - Blood sugars ranged from 100s to 436; she 
was kept on an attenuated followed by her full home lantus dose 
of 28U qhs as her diet improved in addition to sliding scale 
humalog.  She has been seen by ___ on two 
admissions this month, who had been satisfied with her insulin 
regimen.  A1c was 8.3 in ___ and she will follow up with Dr. 
___ at her ___ appointment.
.  
# Hyponatremia - to 130; the patient did not appear dry on exam. 
 BUN was low/nl. Urine concentrated osms with elevated Na; FeNa 
1.3 all suggesting a component of inappropriate ADH in this 
woman with vomiting.  Patient denied headache and was without 
localizing neuro deficits.  TSH and cortisol were wnl on last 
admission and patient was without other signs/sx of 
thyroid/adrenal insufficiency.
.  
# Hypertension - in the setting of nausea and vomiting, managed 
with IV metoprolol while NPO followed by home lisinopril 10 mg 
daily by mouth.

# Sinus tachycardia to 170s in the setting of nausea/vomiting; 
resolved with beta blocker and fluids.  
.  
# Chronic anemia - microcytic.  Patient started on Fe.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ woman with persistent nausea and vomiting.

COMPARISON:  Abdominal radiograph ___.

FINDINGS:  The patient was here for an upper GI small bowel follow-through
study.  However, upon interaction with the patient it was known that the
patient had already had lunch and hence the procedure was scheduled for
tomorrow.

The abdomen radiograph demonstrates nonspecific bowel gas pattern.  No
pneumoperitoneum is identified.  Gastric pacer device is seen overlying the
right upper quadrant.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of bowel obstruction or ileus.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with persistent nausea and vomiting.

FINDINGS:  Single-contrast upper GI exam was performed as the patient could
not do a double contrast exam.  Barium passes freely through the esophagus and
there are normal primary peristaltic contractions.  No hiatal hernia or
gastroesophageal reflux is demonstrated. Stomach distends normally and empties
normally. A gastric pacer is seen in the right lower quadrant. The duodenum,
jejunum and ileum appear normal in caliber, contour and mucosal pattern. 
Barium passes through the small bowel reaching the cecum within three hours.

IMPRESSION:  Normal upper GI and small bowel follow-through, with no evidence
of small bowel pathology.
